top_signals.title: Ebadian: Saudi Private Credit Market Shows Promise
top_signals.summary:
Saudi Arabia could represent a $100 billion opportunity for private credit as the kingdom looks to fund its ambitious economic transformation but turning that potential into deals is proving difficult, with regulatory hurdles, lengthy licensing timelines and a shortage of transactions large enough to attract major global investors. Atefeh Ebadian, Chief Economist & Investment Strategist at Symax Group spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.summary: The French government said that local companies are set to announce 81 new projects on Monday for a total of €14.9 billion ($16.4 billion).

top_signals.title: ‘We have not delivered’: Capita boss quits after Civil Service pensions scheme row
top_signals.summary: The boss of one of the government’s biggest outsourcing partners has quit after the firm warned its botched handling of the civil service pension scheme was continuing to hurt its profit. Adolfo Hernandez has stepped down as chief executive of Capita with immediate effect. He will be replaced by current chief financial officer Pablo Andres. [...]

top_signals.title: Coca-Cola HBC Rises in JSE Debut Ahead of $2.6 Billion Deal
top_signals.summary: Coca-Cola HBC AG rose in its Johannesburg trading debut, adding one of the world’s biggest bottlers of the beverage to Africa’s largest stock exchange days before it completes a $2.6 billion acquisition that will significantly expand its presence on the continent.

top_signals.title: EU Green Energy Giants Slam €40 Billion Budget Cut
top_signals.summary: Companies active in alternative energy and related technology have slammed the EU for plans to reduce the size of the European Competitiveness Fund as part of a broader 40 billion euro (~$44 billion) budget cut. According to the group, featuring 75 companies and industry associations, the European Competitiveness Fund is vital for European businesses if they want to catch up with China and the United States in key industries, Reuters reported, citing a letter penned by the group, which includes energy heavyweights such as France’s EDF.
